title: Rollback & Experiment Visuals: scenarios, microcopy, grooming notes
body:
Goal: capture visual scenarios and microcopy variations for rollback and experiment flows, list groomed backlog items, and surface open questions before design handoff. This is an operational companion doc (working notes + quick wire text) rather than final mockups.

Context and problem statement:
- We already support canary and A/B route targeting. What is missing is a clear, predictable rollback experience when: the canary degrades, an A/B variant fails quality thresholds, or an automatic fallback is triggered. Teams need a) reassuring visuals that explain what changed and why, b) clear microcopy for next actions, and c) telemetry-driven suggestions for rollback vs. partial rollbacks.

Audience:
- Primary: product owners / SREs / ML engineers operating rollouts.
- Secondary: PMs and customer success who will use console screenshots in runbooks.

Key UX goals:
1) Make the active rollout state unambiguous at glance (percentages, time window, signal badges).
2) Surface causal signals (latency, token errors, quality regression score) and recommended actions.
3) Offer safe, fast rollback paths (full rollback, partial % rollback, rollback-to-last-stable) with one-click options and confirm affordances.
4) Communicate automation (automatic-fallback rules) and provide undo.
5) Preserve auditability (who initiated rollback, reason, metrics at time).

High-level visual scenarios to support (wireframe text + notes):
A) Canary degrades during a 30m window
- Top header: "Canary running — 10% traffic (12:13 UTC)" with amber dot and tooltip: "Policy: observe 30m — auto-fallback if error rate > 3%".
- Main column: two-card view: left: "Signals" (latency P95, 500s, quality delta) — show sparklines over 30m; right: "Actions" with primary CTA: "Pause canary" (confirmation), secondary: "Rollback to stable" (one-click with undo for 5 minutes).
- Microcopy for primary CTA tooltip: "Pause routing to this variant immediately. Requests will be routed to the previous stable model until resumed."
- Graceful undo: after rollback, show banner: "Rollback completed — revert?" with a 5-minute timer and button "Revert rollback".

B) A/B test variant fails quality check (automated evaluation)
- Header: "Experiment: A/B prompt-boost — variant B failing quality" (red flag).
- Inline recommendation pill: "Suggest: shift 100% to control (variant A)" with small reasoning: "BLEU -4.2, customer escalation rate +6%".
- Action menu: "Apply suggested shift" (3-step dialog: preview, confirm, deploy).
- Microcopy in dialog: "Shifting traffic will update live routing immediately. You can schedule a canary to re-introduce variant B later."

C) Automatic fallback triggered (region-level capacity)
- System banner: "Automatic fallback: model-cpu-quantized (fallback variant) is serving 60% of requests in eu-west1 due to capacity constraints."
- Visual timeline: show chain-of-events: capacity spike -> fallback applied -> error rate stabilized.
- Microcopy: "Fallback applied automatically by policy. Learn why: capacity exceeded in target pool — read runbook." Link to runbook and show breadcrumbs to adjust policy.

Wireframe components and microcopy drafts (short snippets):
- Status button states: green: "Active (stable)", amber: "Observing (canary)", red: "Degraded". Tooltips: "Active: meets SLOs", "Observing: running canary — auto fallback = ON", "Degraded: metrics outside thresholds".
- Action buttons:
  - "Pause rollout" -> confirmation: "Pause routing to this variant? In-flight requests will finish. You can resume from this screen."
  - "Rollback to last stable" -> confirmation: "Rollback immediately — traffic will switch to last stable variant. This action is auditable and can be undone within 5m."
  - "Scale back to X%" -> inline slider + numeric input, microcopy: "Set percent of traffic for this variant. Use small increments for reducing blast radius."
- Telemetry cards (compact): each card shows metric name, recent delta, and confidence. Example: "Latency P95 — +120ms (high confidence)", link: "see traces".

Backlog grooming (items, acceptance criteria, LOE estimates):
1) Rollback undo window (UX + backend gating) — MED — AC: after a rollback, show 5m undo banner; user can revert to pre-rollback state; audit log entry created; tests for concurrent rollbacks. Linked: JIRA-ENG-1142.
2) Suggested action engine (UI + rules) — HIGH — AC: UI surfaces up to 3 suggested actions based on signal rules; each suggestion includes reason and one-click apply; experiments show >50% acceptance in internal trials.
3) Visual timeline for event chain — LOW — AC: timeline shows last 6 events for rollout with timestamps and links to traces/runbooks.
4) Microcopy variant A/B test for CTAs — LOW — AC: three microcopy variants implemented and measured in usability sessions with 10 operators.
5) Partial rollback slider component (accessibility + keyboard) — MED — AC: slider works with keyboard, readable aria labels, and numeric input available.

Prioritization rationale: items 1 & 2 unblock safe operation and reduce toil; 3 & 4 are nicer-to-have but improve trust; 5 is necessary before exposing percent-rollbacks to SREs.

Open questions to resolve before design handoff:
- Undo semantics: should undo restore the exact routed percentage distribution (if other rollouts changed in the window) or create a new variant that mirrors previous traffic? Needs infra input. Owner: Marco Liu.
- How long should the undo window be configurable per org? Default suggestions: 5m, 15m, 60m. Who can change? (org admins only?)
- Audit UI: do we inline full diffs or link to detailed event logs? Small teams prefer inline; enterprise teams prefer linkouts for retention.

Edge cases and failure modes to call out:
- Two rollbacks initiated concurrently by different users. UX should show a live conflict toast and prevent silent overwrites.
- Rollback when dependent feature flags have changed (model contract mismatch). Provide guardrails preventing rollback if downstream contract incompatible.
- Auto-fallback loops (fallback triggers then now-fallback triggers original variant re-introduction). Add cooldown windows and backoff counters.

Suggested acceptance copy for help text and runbook snippets (ready to paste):
- Runbook banner copy: "Automatic fallback applied: system routed requests to a fallback model because the primary pool breached capacity or quality thresholds. This is reversible from the Rollouts console."
- Confirmation for rollback: "This will update live routing immediately. Traffic will stop going to the current variant and flow to the selected stable variant. This action can be undone for the next 5 minutes."
- Tooltip for suggested action: "Based on observed metrics, we recommend shifting traffic to the previous stable variant to reduce error rate and protect latency SLOs."

Design constraints / accessibility:
- All status colors need non-color cues: icons + text.
- Contrast ratios must meet AA for all banners and CTAs.
- Keyboard flow: primary actions reachable within 3 tab stops; confirmation dialogs trap focus and close with ESC.

Next steps and owners:
- Finalize undo semantics (Marco) — due 2025-11-07
- Prototype microcopy variants and run quick usability test with 6 internal users (Priya) — due 2025-11-14
- Mockup high-fidelity wireframes for the Canary and Experiment screens (Eve + design) — due 2025-11-18
- engineering spike to validate undo backend requirements and conflict resolution (Jonah) — due 2025-11-12

Notes from sync 2025-11-05:
- Eng wants explicit audit record model for rollback with mutation id.
- SRE asked for automated playbook link in every fallback banner.
- Customer-success requested an exportable timeline CSV for customer review.

Attachments/quick sketches (textual):
- sketch-1: header with left status chip, center timeline, right action buttons.
- sketch-2: dialog flow for "Apply suggestion" with three step pills: preview -> verify -> commit.

Status: this is a working draft; please add comments inline in the doc or ping in #prod-rollouts. When we converge on undo semantics, I will convert this into a handoff packet with annotated screens and copy tokens.
